title: Pedestrian zone

paragraphs: Pedestrian zones (also known as auto-free zones and car-free zones, as pedestrian precincts in British English, street malls in  Canada, and as pedestrian malls in the United States and Australia) are areas of a city or town restricted to use by people on foot or human-powered transport such as bicycles, with non-emergency motor traffic not allowed. Converting a street or an area to pedestrian-only use is called pedestrianization.

Pedestrianization usually aims to provide better accessibility and mobility for pedestrians, to enhance the amount of shopping and other business activities in the area or to improve the attractiveness of the local environment in terms of aesthetics, air pollution, noise and crashes involving motor vehicles with pedestrians. In some cases, motor traffic in surrounding areas increases, as it is displaced rather than replaced. Nonetheless, pedestrianisation schemes are often associated with significant falls in local air and noise pollution, better pedestrian safety, and frequently with increased retail turnover and increased property values locally.

A car-free development generally implies a large-scale pedestrianized area that relies on modes of transport other than the car, while pedestrian zones may vary in size from a single square to entire districts, but with highly variable degrees of dependence on cars for their broader transport links.

Pedestrian zones have a great variety of approaches to human-powered vehicles such as bicycles, inline skates, skateboards and kick scooters. Some have a total ban on anything with wheels, others ban certain categories, others segregate the human-powered wheels from foot traffic, and others still have no rules at all. Many Middle Eastern kasbahs have no motorized traffic, but use donkey- or hand-carts to carry goods.

vocabulary.meaning: 步行化；将街道或区域改为步行专用的过程
可达性；方便进入或使用的程度
出行便利程度；移动能力
被转移到别处的，文中指车流转向周边地区
分隔；隔开，文中指分开不同出行人流

questions.prompt: 步行化为何有时会使周边地区的机动车流量增加？
options: 步行区带来零售额增长，因此文中将周边车流增长归因于新增购物者
步行区的划定通常伴随着公共交通服务从周边撤出
原来经过该区域的人力交通改用机动车，增加了周边需求
原有车流可能被转移到周边，而没有真正被其他方式替代
questions.explanation: 第二段指出周边车流在某些情况下会增加，原因是 it is displaced rather than replaced，即车流被转移，而不是被替代。
hints: 区分原因与结果，不要把相关现象直接当作因果。

questions.prompt: 根据最后一段，不同步行区如何管理自行车等人力交通工具？
options: 规则差异很大，可能全面禁行、限制部分种类、分流或不设规则
通常以统一限速为主，较少区分自行车与其他带轮工具
一般按照是否用于运货来管理，而不是按交通工具类型管理
主要采用时间限制，即在营业时段允许与行人混行
questions.explanation: 最后一段列出多种做法：禁止一切带轮工具、禁止某些类别、将轮式人力交通与行人分开，以及完全没有相关规则。
hints: 先确定题干中的对象，再核对原文对它的限定。

sentence.text: In some cases, motor traffic in surrounding areas increases, as it is displaced rather than replaced.
sentence.translation: 在某些情况下，周边地区的机动车流量反而增加，因为车流只是被转移到了别处，而没有被其他出行方式替代。
sentence.analysis: 主干是 motor traffic in surrounding areas increases，句首 In some cases 限定适用情形。as 引导原因状语从句，it 指前面的 motor traffic；is displaced 使用被动语态。rather than 连接 displaced 与 replaced，突出“转移位置”和“被替代”的区别，是解释周边交通增加的关键。
